# GTA6Box

> An independent GTA 6 guide: mission walkthroughs, the Leonida map, characters, cars, weapons, cheats, editions and PC news. Confirmed facts only, updated daily.

GTA6Box is an independent, unofficial fan guide to Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). Each page states whether its information is confirmed by Rockstar Games, lists its sources and shows the date it was last updated. Content may be quoted with a link to the page.

Languages: [English](https://gta6box.com/), [Español](https://gta6box.com/es/), [Português](https://gta6box.com/pt/), [Русский](https://gta6box.com/ru/), [Français](https://gta6box.com/fr/), [Deutsch](https://gta6box.com/de/), [Polski](https://gta6box.com/pl/), [Italiano](https://gta6box.com/it/).

# Does GTA 6 Run at 60 FPS? Graphics and Performance

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-60-fps/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Rockstar confirmed on November 10, 2026 that GTA 6 targets 30 FPS on every console.
- There is no 60 FPS or performance mode at launch, including on PS5 Pro.
- The PS5 Pro gets ray-traced shadows and PSSR upscaling instead.

No, GTA 6 does not run at 60 FPS: it targets 30 frames per second on every console, including the PS5 Pro, and there is no performance mode at launch. Rockstar confirmed the target on November 10, 2026, in the same Newswire post that announced pre-loading. This page sets out what each console gets, why Rockstar chose 30, what critics made of it, which settings make it feel smoother, and where 60 FPS could realistically come from.
Frame-rate targets and PS5 Pro features are as Rockstar announced them, reported by Notebookcheck and other outlets. Anything found in pre-load files is labelled as unofficial.
GTA 6 frame rate at a glance

Console
Frame rate target
60 FPS mode
Extras

PlayStation 5
30 FPS
No
DualSense haptics, Tempest 3D Audio

PS5 Pro
30 FPS
No
Ray-traced shadows, PSSR upscaling

Xbox Series X
30 FPS
No
None listed

Xbox Series S
30 FPS
No
Lower resolution

Rockstar has not published an official resolution table for each console.
What Rockstar confirmed
The November 10 announcement gave one target for the whole generation: 30 FPS on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S. According to Notebookcheck's report, Rockstar tied the decision to keeping the density and visual quality of the open world, and did not rule out further graphics modes later. It also did not promise any.
A target is not a guarantee. Notebookcheck points out that aiming for 30 does not mean the game holds 30 in every scene.
Why it matters: there is no menu choice to make. You will not find a Performance or Quality toggle on any console, so the question of which mode to use does not arise.
What the PS5 Pro adds
The Pro runs at the same 30 FPS target. What it gets instead:

Ray-traced shadows, described as exclusive to the Pro.
PSSR, Sony's upscaling technology, which the base PS5 does not have.

Why it matters: the Pro version should look sharper and more grounded, not smoother. If frame rate is your reason for considering a Pro, GTA 6 does not justify it at launch. The full comparison is in best console for GTA 6.
Base PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
On the base PS5, Rockstar listed DualSense haptic feedback, Tempest 3D Audio and optimised loading. No Xbox-specific features were announced. Rockstar has not said what resolution or which cutbacks the Xbox Series S version uses; Notebookcheck notes only that the console has far less graphics power and memory than the Series X.
The official Extended Look, embedded above, was captured on a base PS5, so it is a fair guide to what that console shows.
Tip: both Xbox consoles and both PlayStations run the same game at the same target. Choose on price, storage and where your friends play; see GTA 6 platforms.
Why 30 FPS
Rockstar's stated reason is the world itself: the number of people, vehicles and animals on screen and the detail they are drawn with. A simulation that dense is limited by the processor as much as by the graphics chip, which is why lowering resolution alone would not double the frame rate.
There is precedent. GTA 5 ran at 30 FPS on the consoles it launched on, and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched at 30 FPS as well. Rockstar's console games have consistently spent their budget on the world first.
Why it matters: the 30 FPS target is a design decision, not a bug waiting for a patch. Expect it to stay through this console generation unless Rockstar says otherwise.
What reviewers said about performance
The frame rate is the most common complaint in reviews of a game that otherwise scored 99 on Metacritic. At least one top-score review listed there names the 30 FPS cap among its few criticisms, and VGC's review mentions minor performance dips while saying they do not spoil the game.
None of the major outlets lowered a score to below 9 because of it. The round-up is in GTA 6 reviews.
Why it matters: if you can play other 30 FPS games comfortably, critics suggest you will stop noticing. If you are used to 60 and sensitive to the difference, expect an adjustment period of an hour or two.
Settings that make 30 FPS feel better
The game has no frame-rate option, but several camera and display settings change how smooth it feels. These names are from the launch options listing:

Setting
Where
Suggestion

Motion Blur Strength
Display &gt; Visual Effects
Keep some on; blur hides the gaps between frames

Camera Shake
Camera
Lower it if fast driving feels juddery

Weapon Sway and Camera Bob
Camera
Lower them for a steadier picture on foot

Aim Response Curve
Controller
Try Linear or Precision if aiming feels sluggish

Stick deadzones
Controller
Reduce slightly for quicker response

And on your television:

Turn on Game Mode to cut input delay.
Switch off motion smoothing; it adds lag and artefacts.
If your TV supports VRR, leave it on. It will not raise the frame rate but can help with consistency.

Tip: change one setting at a time and drive the same stretch of road after each change. More options that affect how the game plays are in GTA 6 difficulty settings.
Could 60 FPS come later?
Rockstar has not announced it. Three routes are possible, and none is confirmed:

A patch. Rockstar did not rule out additional graphics modes, which is not the same as planning one.
A 40 FPS mode. Notebookcheck reports that pre-load metadata contains a reference to 120 Hz output, which led to speculation about a 40 FPS option for 120 Hz screens. The same report says this does not confirm any such mode.
A later version. GTA 5 only received a 60 FPS mode when it was re-released on newer consoles years after launch.

A PC version would be the most likely place for higher frame rates, but it has no date: see GTA 6 on PC and the expected PC requirements.
What is not confirmed

Resolutions. No official native or upscaled figures for any console.
Series S cutbacks. Not disclosed.
A 40 FPS or 120 Hz mode. Datamined hints only.
Measured frame rates. We have not yet seen two independent technical analyses with matching numbers, so we do not quote dips or averages.
Any 60 FPS patch. Not announced.

What to do first

Set your TV to Game Mode and turn off motion smoothing.
Leave motion blur on at first; lower it later if you dislike the look.
Play for an hour before judging. The first minutes after a 60 FPS game are the worst.
If aiming feels heavy, adjust the response curve and deadzones before blaming the frame rate.
Keep the game updated; performance fixes arrive in patches, tracked in GTA 6 updates.

What this means for you
GTA 6 is a 30 FPS game on every console you can buy today, and nothing official suggests that will change soon. That makes the choice of console simpler: none of them is the smooth one. Pick the PS5 Pro for image quality, any other for value, and wait for PC only if 60 FPS matters more to you than playing now.
For what the game looks like in motion, see GTA 6 gameplay.
What we will add to this page

Measured frame rates per console when two technical analyses agree.
Official resolutions if Rockstar publishes them.
Any new graphics mode added by a title update.

Q: Is GTA 6 60 FPS on PS5?
A: No. GTA 6 targets 30 FPS on PS5, and no 60 FPS mode has been announced.

Q: Does GTA 6 run at 60 FPS on PS5 Pro?
A: No. The PS5 Pro targets 30 FPS too, with ray-traced shadows and PSSR upscaling as its extras.

Q: Does GTA 6 have a performance mode?
A: Not at launch. Rockstar has announced one frame rate target for all consoles.

# GTA 6 Afternoon Delight Walkthrough: Rob Vicki's Boss

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-afternoon-delight-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Afternoon Delight is a Chapter 2 main mission from Vicki: rob the safe at Delights, the club where she works.
- The safe code is 2008. Helping the dancers or refusing changes the scenes and objectives, not the outcome.
- Vicki sends $10,000 through BuckMe the next day on either route, the biggest single payout of the chapter.

This GTA 6 Afternoon Delight walkthrough covers the last job before the end of Chapter 2: Vicki wants her boss's safe emptied, and she pays $10,000 for it. The mission has one real decision, and both branches lead to the same safe, the same shootout and the same money. PowerPyx subtitles it Rob Vicki's Boss.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Afternoon Delight (Chapter 2)

Playable characters
Jason and Lucia; either can take the call

Given by
Vicki, by phone

Starts at
Delights, Port Gellhorn

Requirement
Finish Coffee Break, then wait for Vicki's call

Reward
$10,000 via BuckMe the next day

Objectives

Find a way backstage.
Watch the show.
Rob the Delights safe.
Leave Delights.
Escape the bikers.

Step-by-step
1. Get inside
Go to the club. If you arrive alone, your partner is called in. It is ladies' night, so the bouncer lets only Lucia through the front.
As Jason: wait until the two bouncers walk off, climb the fence behind the building and go through the open door. It leads to the male dancers' dressing room, where the lead dancer, Mario, wants Jason to join the act.
2. Help or Don't Help

Help
Don't Help

What happens
Jason dances on stage with Mario and Lucky while Lucia slips to the back office
The dancers quit, Frankie takes the stage, and Jason fires into the ceiling to start the robbery

The safe
Security catches Lucia; Jason rescues her
The two open it together

The chase
Bikers have less time to call reinforcements
Bikers chase more aggressively

Afterwards
You appear at a clothing store to buy Jason clothes, then drive to Vicki
You appear at the docks and hand over the bag in a scene

Length
Longer, with extra scenes and dialogue
Quicker

Both guides say the choice does not change the result. Whichever you pick, you briefly play as Lucia and walk from the bar to the stage.
3. Open the safe
The safe is in the back office. The code is 2008. Opening it alerts every guard in the building.
4. Shoot your way out
Fight to the exit and drive off with the bikers behind you. Both guides call the escape easy.
5. Deliver the bag
Hand the cash to Vicki at the docks, after the clothes stop if Jason danced.
Where players fail

Trying the front door as Jason. Use the fence at the back.
Standing in the open after the safe. Every guard is alerted at once.
Expecting the money immediately. It arrives through BuckMe the next day.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Payment
$10,000 via BuckMe the next day, on either route

Choice
Affects this mission only (GTABase)

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

The payout covers two-thirds of the $15,000 for Prepare for Vice City. Vicki's first appearance is in Girl's Trip. After this, PowerPyx lists only the chapter finale, Checking Out. Order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: What is the safe code in the GTA 6 Afternoon Delight walkthrough?
A: 2008. PowerPyx and GTABase both give the same code for the safe in the back office at Delights.

Q: Should you choose Help or Don't Help in Afternoon Delight?
A: Either. Both guides say the choice affects only this mission. Don't Help is quicker; Help adds scenes, dialogue and an errand to buy Jason clothes.

Q: How does Jason get into Delights?
A: It is ladies' night, so the bouncer only admits Lucia. As Jason, wait for the two bouncers to walk away, climb the fence behind the club and use the open door.

Q: How much does Afternoon Delight pay?
A: $10,000 from Vicki via BuckMe the next day, whichever route you take.

# GTA 6 Behind on Payments Walkthrough: Pay Linda $900

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-behind-on-payments-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Behind on Payments is a Chapter 2 mission with one task: pay Linda $900 for the motel room.
- The quickest honest route is Moses: sell untracked stolen cars, or finish Daily Driver for $1,250 or more.
- Paying returns the necklace Linda was holding as collateral.

This GTA 6 Behind on Payments walkthrough is about money: Lucia owes the Starlet Motel $900 and has to find it. The debt comes from Overnight Charges, where Linda took Lucia's necklace as security. There is no combat and no timer in either guide, so the only question is the fastest way to raise the cash.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Behind on Payments (Chapter 2)

Playable character
Lucia

Given by
Linda

Location
Starlet Motel reception, Kelly County

Requirement
Finish Overnight Charges and have $900

Reward
None listed; the necklace is returned

Objectives

Get $900.
Pay Linda for the motel room.

Step-by-step
1. Raise $900
Both guides recommend doing other missions first rather than grinding.

Method
What you get
Notes

Varies by car

Named by both guides as a way to pay straight away

Store registers
Small amounts

Tip: Lucia begins the chapter with $146 (GTABase) and spends $50 on pills in Girl's Trip, which Vicki refunds. Hold off on the haircut and clothes errands if you want to clear the debt sooner; nothing in the guides says Linda's bill grows while you wait.
2. Pay at reception
With $900 in hand, go to the Starlet Motel reception and talk to Linda. The mission ends when the payment goes through.
3. Collect the necklace
If Linda was holding the necklace, she gives it back.
Where players fail

Arriving with less than $900. Both guides say to talk to Linda only once you have the full amount.
Losing cash on the way. Carried money is at risk if you are wasted or busted; see how the wanted level works.
Robbing stores next to the motel. A wanted level outside reception slows everything down.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Reward
None (PowerPyx)

Returned
Lucia's necklace (GTABase)

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

PowerPyx lists Slam Dunk as the next walkthrough after this one. For more income ideas see how to make money in GTA 6; for the chapter order, the GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you get $900 in the GTA 6 Behind on Payments walkthrough?
A: Play the other Chapter 2 missions first. After the Moses mission you can sell him untracked stolen cars, and Daily Driver pays $1,250. Mugging and store registers also work.

Q: Where do you pay Linda in GTA 6?
A: At the reception desk of the Starlet Motel in Kelly County, once you are carrying $900.

Q: Do you get Lucia's necklace back?
A: Yes. GTABase says the necklace is returned when you pay, if Linda was holding it as collateral.

# GTA 6 Bigfoot: Where to Find the Skunk Ape Near Hamlet

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-bigfoot/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: partly

- The GTA 6 Bigfoot sighting is at Cottonmouth Lake, just below Hamlet, and is available as soon as you can drive freely.
- The creature stands over a carcass on the road and runs into the marsh; waiting by the flowers near its effigy triggers a short scene.
- VGC reports that the game calls it the Skunk Ape and that a character called Kirk later starts a questline for Jason; that part has one source so far.

The GTA 6 Bigfoot sighting is at Cottonmouth Lake, just below Hamlet, and you can drive there almost as soon as the game lets you roam. Players found it on launch day. What you meet is brief and strange: a large hairy figure on the road, a chase you will lose, and a scene that ends before you get a proper look. This page explains where to go, what happens, what the game itself calls the creature, and which parts of the story are still reported by only one guide.
The location and the encounter are described the same way by two independent guides. The name Skunk Ape and the follow-up questline come from VGC alone and are marked that way below.
GTA 6 Bigfoot at a glance

Question
Answer
Sources

Where?
Cottonmouth Lake, just below Hamlet
Insider Gaming, Critical Hits

When can you go?
As soon as you can drive freely
Insider Gaming, Critical Hits

How do you know you are close?
A deep, guttural growl
Insider Gaming, Critical Hits

What do you see?
A creature over an animal carcass on the road; it runs into the marsh
Insider Gaming, Critical Hits

What is it called in the game?
The Skunk Ape, according to locals
VGC

Is there a reward?
None reported
All three

Is there more?
A questline for Jason, started by a man called Kirk
VGC only

Where to find it
Drive to Cottonmouth Lake. Both location guides describe it the same way: just below Hamlet in Vice Dale County. Hamlet Correctional, the prison where the Prologue begins, takes its name from the same town. If you need bearings, our GTA 6 map guide covers the regions.
VGC describes the trigger from a different angle: most players see the creature while driving towards the Kingfishers' camp near the water south of Hamlet. The Kingfishers' swamp shack south-west of Hamlet is where the story sends Jason in Clean Up After Donnie, so many players pass through the area early. VGC does not name the lake, so we cannot say for certain that the two descriptions are the same spot, only that both are on the water south of Hamlet.
Tip: go on a clear run without a wanted level, and keep the radio down. The growl is the cue both guides give for being in the right place.
What happens when you get there
Insider Gaming and Critical Hits give the same sequence:

The creature is on the road, standing over the body of an animal.
When you approach, it runs into the marshland beside the road. You can follow, but both guides say you will probably lose it.
Where it was standing, an odd effigy is tied to a tree.
If you stay near the flowers there, they appear to knock your character out.
A unique scene plays: you drift in and out of consciousness, the creature comes close, and all you see is a pair of large, hairy feet.

Why it matters: the scene by the flowers is the real payoff, and it is easy to miss if you sprint after the creature and never come back to the tree. Let it run, then wait.
Is it actually Bigfoot?
Not according to VGC, which puts the name in quotation marks in its headline for that reason. Its guide says the creature in the widely shared clip is a character that locals call the Skunkape, and that posters of it can be seen around Key Lento near the start of the game.
That fits the setting. The skunk ape is Florida's own version of the Bigfoot legend, a swamp creature of local folklore, and Leonida is Rockstar's version of Florida. The other two guides use Bigfoot or Sasquatch and do not mention the posters.
Why it matters: if you search the in-game world for "Bigfoot" you will find nothing by that name. Look for Skunk Ape posters instead.
The posters and the second trigger
VGC describes a second way to reach the sighting: find enough of the Skunk Ape posters around town, and the game places a marker on your map in the general area of the first sighting. The guide does not say how many posters count as enough.
Tip: the posters are around Key Lento, where Jason spends much of Chapter 1. If you are still early in the story, keep an eye out for them on your way between missions; the full early order is in the GTA 6 mission list.
The questline: Kirk and the hunt
This section rests on a single source, VGC, so treat it as reported and not yet confirmed.
According to that guide, the sighting is the first step of something longer. After you have seen the creature, let a few in-game days pass. A man called Kirk, described as the leading expert on the creature, then contacts you and asks for help tracking it, which adds a marker to the map. VGC says the questline can only be started as Jason, and only at night. Its coverage of the questline itself is in a separate guide marked for spoilers.
Insider Gaming and Critical Hits were written a little earlier and both say it was unclear whether the sighting was a one-off or the start of something bigger. VGC's report answers that question, but until a second guide describes Kirk's missions we are not listing them.
Why it matters: if you are playing as Lucia in Chapter 2 and nothing happens after the sighting, that may be why. Switch to Jason once switching unlocks; see how to switch characters in GTA 6.
Rewards: what you get and what you do not
No guide reports a cash reward, a trophy, a collectible or a challenge for the sighting. Critical Hits says outright not to expect one. Our pages on GTA 6 collectibles and the trophy guide do not list anything tied to it either.
Why it matters: this is an easter egg in the old sense, worth doing for the scene. It will not move your completion percentage as far as anyone has shown.
Bigfoot in earlier GTA games

Game
Bigfoot

GTA: San Andreas
A long-running fan myth; never in the game

GTA 5
Appears briefly in the story mission Predator; the re-release hid further Sasquatch secrets that took players years to solve

GTA 6
A roadside sighting at launch, with a questline reported

Rockstar has played with the legend for two decades, mostly by teasing. In GTA 6 the creature was found on launch day, on a public road, by players who were not even looking for it. That is a change of approach: the secret here is not whether it exists but what it wants.
What is not confirmed

Kirk's questline. Its missions, length and rewards. One source so far.
The night-only condition. VGC's wording leaves it unclear whether night applies to Kirk's call or to starting the quest.
The number of posters needed for the map marker.
Whether the sighting repeats. No guide says if the creature can be seen there again.
Other locations. Insider Gaming says more may be found elsewhere and that it will update if so.
Whether the two descriptions of the place match exactly. Cottonmouth Lake in two guides; the approach to the Kingfishers' camp in the third.

How to see it: step by step

Play until you can drive around freely.
Open the map and set a waypoint at Cottonmouth Lake, below Hamlet.
Drive slowly along the road by the water and listen for the growl.
Stop when you see the figure over the carcass. Approach on foot.
Let it run. Do not waste time on the chase.
Find the effigy on the tree where it stood.
Stand by the flowers and wait for the scene.
Afterwards, carry on with the story and, as Jason, watch your phone over the next few in-game days.

Make a manual save first if you want to be able to watch it again: how to save in GTA 6.
What this means for you
It takes a few minutes and costs nothing, and it is one of the more memorable things in the opening hours, so it is worth the detour the next time you are near Hamlet. Do not expect a prize. If VGC's report holds up, the sighting is also the door to a longer hunt, and seeing it early means Kirk's call can arrive sooner.
For the real wildlife of Leonida, more than 170 species of it, see GTA 6 animals. For other optional characters, see GTA 6 Strangers and Freaks.
What we will add to this page

Kirk's questline, step by step, once a second guide confirms it.
The poster locations and how many are needed.
Any reward, trophy or cheat linked to the hunt.
Other sightings, if players find the creature elsewhere on the map.

Q: Where is Bigfoot in GTA 6?
A: At Cottonmouth Lake, just below Hamlet. Two guides give the same spot and say a deep growl tells you that you are close.

Q: Is it really Bigfoot in GTA 6?
A: VGC says no: locals in the game call the creature the Skunk Ape, and posters of it hang around Key Lento. Other guides simply call it Bigfoot or Sasquatch.

Q: Do you get a reward for finding Bigfoot in GTA 6?
A: No guide reports a reward, trophy or collectible for the sighting itself. One guide says explicitly not to expect one.

Q: When can you find Bigfoot in GTA 6?
A: Early. Two guides say you can go as soon as the game lets you drive around freely, without much story progress.

# GTA 6 Boobie Time Walkthrough: Seashark Chase and Yasmani

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-boobie-time-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Boobie Time is a Jason-only Chapter 3 mission from Boobie Ike that starts at the Jack of Hearts in Crosstown.
- Thieves take the cash bag and Jason chases them down the river on a Seashark; ride over the bag to pick it up.
- It unlocks Yasmani, a fence who pays more for jewelry and marked bills than the other drop-offs.

This GTA 6 Boobie Time walkthrough covers a driving job for Boobie Ike that turns into a river chase, and ends by introducing the best fence for jewelry in the game. The unlock is the reason to do it early. PowerPyx subtitles it Talk to Boobie.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Boobie Time (Chapter 3)

Playable character
Jason only

Given by
Boobie Ike

Starts at
Jack of Hearts, Crosstown, Vice City

Requirement
Part 1 of Dubious Provenance

Reward
Yasmani unlocked as a goods drop-off

Objectives

Get in Boobie's car.
Go to the pick-up location.
Go to the club.
Retrieve the cash bag.
Return to Boobie.
Get in your car.
Go to the smoke shop.
Enter the smoke shop.

Step-by-step
1. Drive Boobie
Follow Boobie out of the club and take the driver's seat of his car.
2. Two pickups

First stop: a few blocks south. Wait while Boobie talks to the men in the parking lot.
Second stop: a short drive south-west. Pull up, press L3 to honk and wait while he talks to the man on the stairs.

3. The club by the river
Drive south to the city centre and stop beside the building near the river.
4. Chase the bag
After the scene inside, thieves take the cash bag from the car. Jason follows on a Seashark automatically. Chase them down the river; you can shoot as you ride.
Tip: you do not need to hit them at speed. Both guides say the thieves end up in a dead end and circle while shooting, which makes them much easier targets.
When they are down, ride over the bag and press Triangle (Y on Xbox) to pick it up.
5. Back to Boobie
Ride back up the river, get off the Seashark and return to Boobie's car.
6. Meet Yasmani
Drive a short way across the river to the smoke shop and go inside with Boobie. He introduces Yasmani, and the mission ends.
Where players fail

Wasting ammo during the chase. Wait for the dead end.
Missing the bag. It floats where the thieves went down; you have to ride over it and press the button.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Unlock
Yasmani as a drop-off for goods

Why it matters
He pays more for jewelry and marked bills than the other drop-offs (both guides)

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

Yasmani gets in touch afterwards about three stores; see Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs. If you are holding jewelry from Chapter 2 jobs such as Hit Avery Pawn, this is the place to sell it. More in how to make money in GTA 6. Full order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you start the GTA 6 Boobie Time walkthrough mission?
A: Finish the first part of Dubious Provenance, then go to the Jack of Hearts in Crosstown as Jason.

Q: How do you get the cash bag back in Boobie Time?
A: Follow the thieves down the river on the Seashark. They stop in a dead end and circle, which makes them easier to hit. Then ride over the bag and press Triangle on PS5 or Y on Xbox.

Q: What does Boobie Time unlock?
A: Yasmani as a goods drop-off. PowerPyx and GTABase both say he pays more for jewelry and marked bills than other fences.

Q: What comes after Boobie Time?
A: Yasmani contacts you about three store robberies, covered in our Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs walkthrough.

# GTA 6 Breakfast Run Walkthrough: The Store Robbery Spree

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-breakfast-run-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Breakfast Run starts about half a day after Slam Dunk, when Jason calls and the motel icon turns pink.
- Jason and Lucia rob a diner, a liquor store and a thrift store back to back; each robbery has a one-minute timer.
- It ends with a two-star wanted level, unlocks the Trust trophy and makes Jason playable again.

This GTA 6 Breakfast Run walkthrough covers the mission where Jason gets back on his feet and the couple go straight back to work. It is a chain of quick store robberies that teaches the hold-up system you will use for money for the rest of the game. PowerPyx subtitles it Check on Jason.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Breakfast Run (Chapter 2)

Playable character
Lucia, with Jason alongside

Given by
Jason and Lucia

Starts at
Starlet Motel, Kelly County (pink icon)

Requirement
Finish Slam Dunk, then wait for Jason's call

Reward
Trust trophy; Jason playable again

Objectives

Go to Hank's Waffles.
Rob the diner.
Rob the liquor store.
Rob the thrift store.
Get in the car.
Lose the cops.

Step-by-step
1. Take Jason's call
The call comes roughly half a day after Slam Dunk. Both guides say finishing other open missions helps bring it on. Go back to the motel room; a scene shows time passing until Jason has healed, and the two decide to rob some stores.
2. Drive to Hank's Waffles
Follow the marker to the waffle house.
3. Rob the diner

Step
What to do

Threaten
Aim your gun at the staff and use the threaten prompt (Square on PS5, X on Xbox, per PowerPyx)

Collect
They open the register and put cash on the counter; pick it up

Leave
A one-minute timer runs in the bottom-right corner; walk out before it ends

When you leave, the game moves you straight to the next store.
4. Liquor store and thrift store
You appear inside the liquor store. Aim at the clerk, take the money and get in the car, which takes you to the thrift store. Repeat.
Jason and Lucia then hit a gas station and another liquor store by themselves.
5. Lose the cops
Back at the car you have a two-star wanted level. Both guides recommend the small off-road trails as the easiest way out. See how the wanted level works.
6. Back at the motel
A scene returns you to the Starlet Motel for the night. In the morning Vicki comes for her laptop, and the story runs directly into Coffee Break.
Where players fail

Letting the timer run down. Threaten, grab the cash and go; do not browse.
Staying on main roads with two stars. Take the dirt trails.
Expecting free roam afterwards. Coffee Break starts immediately.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Trophy
Trust (both guides)

Jason
Playable again

Personal vehicles
One each for Jason and Lucia (PowerPyx)

Take Care of Jason
The background mission Take Care of Jason completes after this one

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

Neither guide lists how much the robberies pay. Hold-ups as a way to earn are covered in how to make money in GTA 6. Chapter order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you start the GTA 6 Breakfast Run walkthrough?
A: Finish Slam Dunk and wait for Jason's call, which takes about half a day of in-game time. Then return to the room at the Starlet Motel; its icon turns pink.

Q: How do you rob the stores in Breakfast Run?
A: Aim your gun at the staff and use the threaten prompt (Square on PS5, X on Xbox, per PowerPyx). They put the cash on the counter; grab it and leave before the one-minute timer runs out.

Q: What does Breakfast Run unlock in GTA 6?
A: The Trust trophy or achievement, and Jason as a playable character again. PowerPyx adds that Jason and Lucia each have a personal vehicle afterwards.

# How Much Did GTA 6 Cost to Make?

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-budget/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: partly

- Rockstar and Take-Two have never published a budget for GTA 6.
- Analyst estimates reported in 2026 put development at about $1 billion to $1.5 billion.
- GTA 5 reportedly cost about $265 million including marketing.

The GTA 6 budget has never been published: Take-Two has only said the game was expensive, and the figure most often quoted, $1 billion to $1.5 billion, is an analyst estimate. Higher numbers exist, and so do lower ones for older games, but none of them comes from the company's accounts. This page sorts the figures by where they come from, explains why they differ, and sets them beside what the game has to earn.
Every number below is attributed to the outlet or person who gave it. Nothing here is an official budget, because there is none.
GTA 6 budget figures at a glance

Figure
Source
What it covers
Status

No figure
Take-Two Interactive
n/a
Official position: not disclosed

$1 billion to $1.5 billion
Industry analysts quoted by Business Insider, May 2026
Development; reports say it probably excludes marketing
Estimate

About $2 billion
Josh Chapman of Konvoy, cited by PC Gamer
Total investment assumed for a break-even model
Estimate

More than $2 billion in salaries
UK public records, as reported by GamingBolt
Staff pay only
Unverified; not confirmed by Rockstar or Take-Two

$3.4 billion
Dan Dawkins, cited by PC Gamer
Includes pre-production and Rockstar payroll over six years
Estimate

What Take-Two has actually said
Chief executive Strauss Zelnick has been asked about the cost several times in 2026 and has never given a number.

To Business Insider in May, he said the game was expensive, as GamingBolt and Gfinity both report.
In a Bloomberg interview the same month, covered by PC Gamer, he said development costs keep rising and that AI has not yet brought them down, and described spending at this level as a bet for "big boys only" that he is comfortable with.
Destructoid reports that on CNBC he called production costs high, said the figure has not been disclosed, and said the company "seeks perfection".

Take-Two does not break out budgets for individual games in its financial reports. Gfinity notes that the company has never confirmed a budget for Red Dead Redemption 2 either.
Why it matters: any headline that says "GTA 6 cost $X" is quoting someone outside the company. The honest answer to the question is a range with a label on each end.
The analyst estimate: $1 billion to $1.5 billion
This is the range you will see most. It comes from unnamed industry analysts who spoke to Business Insider in May 2026. GamingBolt's report says it probably leaves out marketing, and PC Gamer describes it as the low end of the estimates in circulation.
Why it matters: if marketing is excluded, the total spend to get the game onto shelves would be higher than this range even if the analysts are right about development.
The higher estimates: $2 billion and above
Three larger figures are in circulation, and they measure different things.

About $2 billion. PC Gamer cites Josh Chapman of the investment firm Konvoy, who used it as the budget in a model of how quickly the game pays for itself.
More than $2 billion in salaries. GamingBolt reports this from UK public records and notes that neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has confirmed it and that it contradicts the analyst range.
$3.4 billion. PC Gamer cites an estimate from Dan Dawkins that counts pre-production and Rockstar's payroll across six years.

Tip: when you compare figures, check three things: does it include marketing, does it include pre-production, and does it count all of Rockstar's staff costs or only the GTA 6 team? The spread from $1 billion to $3.4 billion is mostly a disagreement about what to count.
How it compares with other games

Game
Reported cost
Note

GTA 5 (2013)
About $265 million
Widely quoted estimate for development and marketing

Red Dead Redemption 2 (2018)
$350 million to $550 million
Estimates, per Destructoid; never confirmed

Cyberpunk 2077
About $526 million
As listed by Gfinity

GTA 6 (2026)
$1 billion to $1.5 billion or more
Analyst estimates

Gfinity's summary is that GTA 6 cost more than four times as much as GTA 5 at the low end of the estimate. Even that low end would put it among the most expensive entertainment products ever made.
Why it cost so much

Time. Thirteen years separate GTA 5 and GTA 6. First work dates back to 2015 and most of the team joined after 2018; see how long GTA 6 was in development.
Scale. A whole state to explore, about twice the size of GTA 5's map according to Rockstar; see GTA 6 map size.
Density. More than 170 animal species, far more interiors and a story of about 80 hours by one Rockstar studio head's own playthrough; see how long is GTA 6.
Talent and music. Full performance capture for the cast and a licensed soundtrack with well-known radio hosts; see GTA 6 radio stations.
People. Rockstar's studios around the world worked on it, and salaries over many years are the largest cost in any of the estimates.
Delays. The game moved twice before landing on November 19, 2026, and every extra month is another month of payroll; see GTA 6 delays.

Why it matters: none of these costs is unusual on its own. What is unusual is all of them at once, for this long.
What it has to earn back
The Standard Edition costs $79.99; prices for every edition are in GTA 6 price and editions.
Two forecasts frame the other side of the ledger:

Destructoid reports that Take-Two told investors it expects about $8 billion in revenue in fiscal 2027, the year that includes the game's release. That is a company-wide figure.
PC Gamer cites Chapman's projection of roughly $7.6 billion in revenue within 60 days of launch, with break-even inside a month on a $2 billion budget. That is one analyst's model.

Why it matters: on any of the estimates above, the game is expected to cover its cost quickly. The early sales picture, with estimates labelled as estimates, is in how much money has GTA 6 made.
What is not confirmed

Any official budget. Take-Two has not published one and has not said it will.
The marketing spend. No source gives a reliable figure.
The UK salary figure. It is reported from public records but not confirmed by the companies.
Team size. None of the reports we checked gives a verified headcount for GTA 6.
Whether it is the most expensive game ever. Probably, if the estimates are right, but it cannot be proved without the real number.

How to read a new budget headline

Find the source. Is it Take-Two, a named analyst, or "reports"?
Check the scope: development only, development plus marketing, or all Rockstar payroll.
Check the date. Estimates from before the final delay will be low.
Compare it with the ranges in the table at the top of this page.
Treat any single precise number with suspicion; the people who know have not said.

What this means for you
For players, the budget changes nothing about the game on your console. It matters as context: it helps explain the $79.99 price and the long wait, and why so much attention is on launch sales.
What we will add to this page

Any figure Take-Two discloses in an earnings report or filing.
New named-analyst estimates, with their scope.
Official sales and revenue numbers as they are reported, to set against the cost.

Q: How much did GTA 6 cost to make?
A: There is no official figure. Analyst estimates reported in May 2026 range from about $1 billion to $1.5 billion.

Q: Is GTA 6 the most expensive game ever made?
A: If the estimates are right, yes. But the estimates are not confirmed by Take-Two.

Q: Did GTA 6 cost $2 billion?
A: That figure is unverified. Higher numbers usually add marketing to development and are not from Take-Two.

# GTA 6 Car Service Walkthrough: Steal the Schafter V12

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-car-service-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Car Service is a Lucia-only Chapter 3 mission from Raul: steal a Schafter V12 from a gang chop shop in Salton.
- A nearby car trunk holds flash grenades and a silenced Klose K17; the quiet route is over the white van on the north side.
- Delivering the car to Leonida Auto World pays $3,000 and unlocks Randy as a vehicle drop-off.

This GTA 6 Car Service walkthrough covers Raul's test for Lucia: take one car out of a guarded chop shop and deliver it across the city. It can be done without a shot if you use the roof. PowerPyx subtitles it Steal The Car for Raul.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Car Service (Chapter 3)

Playable character
Lucia only

Given by
Raul, by message from a blocked number

Starts at
Salton, south Vice City

Requirement
Meet the Heders, then about a day's wait

Reward
$3,000; Randy unlocked as a vehicle drop-off

Objectives

Search the chop shop for the Schafter V12.
Steal the Schafter V12.
Escape the area.
Deliver the car to Leonida Auto World.

Step-by-step
1. Take the gear
Raul's contact has left equipment in the trunk of a car near the start: flash grenades and a silenced Klose K17 pistol. Taking them is optional, and both guides recommend the silenced pistol.
2. Go over the roof
Climb onto the white van on the north side of the chop shop and step across to the metal roof. Walk around the edge of the yard to see who is where.

Who
Where

Two gang members
Loading a van in the middle of the yard

Two guards
Left and right of the entry gates

A dog
Usually beside one of the gate guards

If one of them is shot and the others notice, they open fire and more men arrive at the gates by car.
Tip: leave the dog alone unless it attacks. Both guides say harming it hurts your criminal rating.
3. Steal the car
The Schafter V12 is parked in the middle of the covered area, next to a small room. Get in and drive out.
4. Escape
Leave before the police arrive. If they do see you, you have to lose them before the delivery marker works. See GTA 6 wanted level.
5. Deliver to Leonida Auto World
The dealership is in the far north-west corner of the city. Driving into the car park starts the closing scene, in which the dealer, Randy, offers to buy high-end vehicles from you.
Where players fail

Going in through a gate. That walks you into both guards and the dog.
Firing an unsilenced weapon. Reinforcements arrive by car.
Driving to the dealership with police behind you. Lose them first.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Payment
$3,000

Unlock
Randy as a drop-off for vehicles with standard trackers and for cars on his request list

Also
Wanted areas in Port Gellhorn and Key Lento cleared (PowerPyx only)

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

Randy is the second way to sell cars, after Pay 'n' Spray opens in Welcome to Vice City. See GTA 6 cars and how to make money in GTA 6. PowerPyx lists First Impressions, the first meeting with Raul, as the mission this one unlocks; we will add it once a second guide confirms the details. Full order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you start the GTA 6 Car Service walkthrough mission?
A: Finish Meet the Heders, then wait about a day. Raul messages Lucia from a blocked number and a marker appears in Salton, in the south of Vice City.

Q: Where is the Schafter V12 in Car Service?
A: In the middle of the covered area of the chop shop, next to a small room.

Q: Should you shoot the dog in Car Service?
A: No, unless it attacks you. Both guides warn that hurting it counts against your criminal rating.

Q: What does Car Service unlock?
A: $3,000 and Randy at Leonida Auto World as a drop-off for vehicles. PowerPyx adds that the wanted areas in Port Gellhorn and Key Lento are cleared.

# GTA 6 Cheats: All 61 Cheats, Codes and How to Unlock Them

URL: https://gta6box.com/cheats/gta-6-cheats/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: partly

- GTA 6 has 61 cheats in five groups; button codes are published for 18 of them so far.
- Cheats unlock only after the main story (reported as 91 missions), and each cheat has its own unlock task.
- The money cheat is Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right for $250,000. Cheats switch off saving and trophies.

GTA 6 has 61 cheats, but none of them work until you finish the story. They come in five groups: player, combat, vehicle spawns, world and screen filters. Each one also has its own unlock task, such as shooting-range medals, races or collectibles. Button codes have been published for 18 cheats so far; the rest are listed below with their unlock tasks, and we add each code as soon as two independent sources agree on it. Rockstar has not released an official list, so this page is marked partly confirmed.
How to enter cheats in GTA 6

Finish the main story. Launch guides report 91 story missions; the Cheats section appears under the Progress tab after the credits.
Complete the unlock task for the cheat you want.
Save your game. Cheats turn saving off.
In free roam, press Up on the D-pad to open the phone.
Hold L1 + R1 on PS5 or LB + RB on Xbox Series X|S. Guides differ on the wording: some say to hold L1 (LB) first and then press R1 (RB).
Enter the code on the D-pad.

All codes use only the D-pad, so they are the same on PS5 and Xbox.
Code patterns

Vehicle spawn codes start with Left, Up, Right, Down.
The three ammo cheats share the opening Down, Up, Right, Down, Left, Left, Up.
The screen filter codes start with Down, Down, Up, Right, Right, Up, Left, Left.

Checked on November 20: still 18 confirmed codes
We compared seven code lists again the day after launch. The 18 codes above match on every list that includes them, and none of the lists contradicts another.

Drunk. A code for the Drunk cheat now appears on two sites, but one of them says the input comes from a single outlet's guide and is not widely corroborated. That is one source, not two, so it stays off the table until an independent guide or Rockstar confirms it.
Raise Wanted Level. Its code is on four lists. Three other guides still mark it as not found, so treat it as the least certain of the 18.
Cycle Weather. The code is agreed. The unlock task is not: guides say either finishing the story or revealing the whole map.
Everything else. No code has been published for the other 42 cheats.

Second check, later on November 20
We ran the comparison again against three more lists: GTABase, Beebom (updated November 19) and Red Bull. All three show the same 18 codes, input for input, and all three still mark the other 43 cheats as "to be announced", including Drunk. Nothing was added to or removed from the tables above.
Two details from that check:

Cycle Weather. All three lists give "finish the story" as the unlock task, which is now the more widely reported version.
Story length. The lists disagree on how many missions stand between you and the Cheats menu: Red Bull says 91, Beebom says 118. The condition itself, finishing the main story, is the same everywhere.

Beebom alone says a cheat can be switched off by entering its code again. One source is not enough, so treat that as unconfirmed.
Checked on November 21: no new codes
Two days after launch the count has not moved. GTABase's list, read again today, still shows 61 cheats with 18 codes and marks the other 43 as "to be announced". Its 18 codes are the same as ours, input for input, and so are the unlock tasks.
Beebom's list, updated on November 20 and read again in a second check today, agrees: 61 cheats, the same 18 codes, 43 still to be announced.
Two details from GTABase are worth knowing, although we have not yet seen a second guide state them:

Entering the code of a cheat you have not unlocked does nothing.
Saving stays off until you quit, so progress made after a cheat is lost when you leave; loading the earlier save restores trophies.

Third check on November 21: Drunk still unconfirmed
A later comparison the same day looked at four lists again.

GTABase and KeenGamer still give no code for Drunk. GTABase shows 18 codes; KeenGamer shows 17 and marks Raise Wanted Level as undiscovered.
GTABoom now counts 19 codes because it includes an input for Drunk. Its other 18 match ours input for input.
Dexerto shows an input for Drunk as well, but we could not read its table cleanly enough to compare every direction, and we noted earlier that the Drunk input traces back to a single outlet.

That is not two independent sources we can check against each other, so Drunk stays out of the table. No code was added, removed or changed today. Two lists also repeat the rule that saving stays off until you quit: GTABase and KeenGamer both say to save first and quit without saving to get trophies back.
If you want to work towards the partner-based filters (Golden Hour, Dollhouse, Videotape, Faded Glory and Pinhole), see GTA 6 romance for what counts as time together.
What cheats switch off

Saving is disabled while a cheat is active.
Trophies and achievements cannot be earned in that session.
Cheats are for story mode free roam only.

Tips for unlocking cheats faster

Many unlock tasks count progress you make during the story, so play shooting ranges, races and workouts as you go.
Do challenge groups in pairs: five challenges unlock one vehicle, all of them unlock a second.
Unlock tasks that need your partner (hours together, store robberies, activities) are easiest to finish in free roam after the credits.

How we check this page

The list of 61 cheats and their unlock tasks matches across several independent launch guides.
A code is listed only when at least two independent guides show the same inputs.
The status stays "partly confirmed" until each code is entered in the released game. If a patch changes a code, we update the table and the date at the top.

Looking for the money code on its own? See GTA 6 money cheat. For police levels, see GTA 6 wanted level.

Q: Does GTA 6 have cheat codes?
A: Yes, according to early guides published the day before launch: 61 cheats, entered with the D-pad through the in-game phone. Rockstar has not published an official list.

Q: What is the GTA 6 money cheat?
A: Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right gives $250,000. It is reported to unlock after you finish the main story.

Q: Can you use cheats from the start of GTA 6?
A: No. The Cheats menu is reported to appear only after the main story is finished, and many cheats need an extra task, such as shooting-range medals or workouts.

Q: How many cheats are in GTA 6?
A: 61: 10 player cheats, 9 combat cheats, 21 vehicle spawns, 3 world cheats and 18 screen filters.

Q: Do cheats disable trophies and achievements in GTA 6?
A: Yes. Reports say an active cheat disables saving and blocks trophies and achievements for that session, so save first.

# GTA 6 Checking Out Walkthrough: The Chapter 2 Finale

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-checking-out-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Checking Out is the last mission of Chapter 2 and a point of no return: the Starlet Motel stops being your home.
- It needs $15,000 and every other Chapter 2 main mission finished, and starts at the bathroom door in your motel room.
- Dying during the bike chase can break the objective; both guides say to restart the mission if that happens.

This GTA 6 Checking Out walkthrough covers the Chapter 2 finale: a shootout at the Starlet Motel, a bike chase and the drive into Vice City. It is short, but it closes the chapter behind you, so the most useful part of this page is the checklist before you start. PowerPyx subtitles the mission Move to Vice City.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Checking Out (Chapter 2 finale)

Playable characters
Jason first, then Lucia

Starts at
Your room at the Starlet Motel, Kelly County

Requirement
$15,000 from Prepare for Vice City and all other Chapter 2 main missions

Reward
None (PowerPyx)

Next
Welcome to Vice City, the start of Chapter 3

Point of no return checklist
Both guides warn that starting the mission ends Chapter 2 and takes the motel away as a home. Before you touch the bathroom door:

Make a manual save in a spare slot. Missions cannot be replayed; see how to save in GTA 6.
Finish the optional jobs you care about: Thrillbillies, Hit Avery Pawn, Hit Kingpin Bowling and Impounded Vehicle.
Stock up as Jason. GTABase notes he may be short on healing items if you mostly played Lucia in this chapter.

Objectives
PowerPyx lists five; GTABase merges two of them and adds a "start the mission" step.

Regroup with Lucia.
Defend yourself.
Follow Jason.
Jump to the car.
Escape with Jason.

Step-by-step
1. Start at the bathroom door
Once the requirements are met, your partner calls about an article Cal sent and the motel is marked on the map. Go to your room and interact with the bathroom door.
2. Regroup with Lucia
Pick up the shotgun from the bed. Corrupt cops have found the motel. Fight through them to the cafeteria at the side of the building, where Lucia is waiting.
Tip: GTABase suggests using any frag grenades you have saved if Jason is low on supplies.
3. Defend yourself
The game switches you to Lucia. Keep shooting while Jason heads for the road and takes a car.
4. Follow Jason on the bike
A biker rides at Lucia. Shoot him, take his bike and follow Jason, who shows as a pink dot on the minimap. Ride cleanly: a crash can throw you off.
5. Jump to the car
When the prompt appears, pull alongside and hold Square on PS5 or X on Xbox to jump across.
6. Escape
Jason drives. As Lucia, shoot at the police cars behind you; both guides say to aim for the tires. A scene follows, and you drive into Vice City.
Where players fail

Dying on the bike. This is the known bug: Jason can disappear as an objective and leave you in a police search area with no way out. Both guides give the same fix, which is to restart the mission.
Crashing during the chase. Stay on the road and keep the pink dot in sight rather than cutting corners.
Starting too early. Anything tied to the motel and Chapter 2 is gone once the mission begins.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Payment
None

Choice
GTABase says you can drive off without Lucia, which hurts the pair's relationship. PowerPyx does not mention it.

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

Unlocks
Chapter 3 and Vice City

For what the relationship level affects, see GTA 6 romance. The story continues in Welcome to Vice City. Full order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you start the GTA 6 Checking Out walkthrough mission?
A: Have $15,000 and finish the other Chapter 2 main missions. Your partner calls about an article Cal sent, the motel is marked, and you interact with the bathroom door in your room.

Q: Is Checking Out a point of no return in GTA 6?
A: Yes. PowerPyx and GTABase both say starting it ends Chapter 2 and removes the Starlet Motel as your home for good.

Q: What is the Checking Out bug in GTA 6?
A: If you die during the bike chase, Jason can vanish as an objective and leave you inside a police search area you cannot escape. Restart the mission and avoid dying on the bike.

Q: Does Checking Out pay anything?
A: No. PowerPyx lists the reward as none. The mission moves the story to Vice City and Chapter 3.

This GTA 6 Coffee Break walkthrough is short, but the mission is the turning point of Chapter 2: it gives you both leads at once. After a $2 coffee, Jason and Lucia agree to raise money for a move to Vice City, and the game unlocks character switching and a set of jobs to fund it.

# GTA 6 Daily Driver Walkthrough: Steal the '82 Crawler

- Daily Driver is Moses's second job in Chapter 2: steal an '82 Canis Crawler, a white jeep, and bring it to his garage.
- The car is guarded; sneak to it or shoot your way in, then drive off.

This GTA 6 Daily Driver walkthrough shows where to find the '82 Crawler and how to collect the full $1,750. Moses wants the jeep taken back from clients who did not pay him. It is a short theft with armed company, and it is the best-paid job available at this point in Chapter 2. PowerPyx lists it as Steal the Crawler for Moses.

# GTA 6 Dealer's Choice Walkthrough: Cut or Pure?

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-dealers-choice-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Dealer's Choice is a Jason-only Chapter 3 mission from Dre'Quan that starts at the Jack of Hearts.
- Tyrone offers Cut or Pure product. Buyers spot Cut, but you can offer half price and still walk away with the money.
- Both guides say the choice affects this mission only; settling the deal without violence earns a Professional bonus.

This GTA 6 Dealer's Choice walkthrough covers Jason's first job in Vice City: a pickup and a sale with Dre'Quan as backup. Boobie Ike calls it a favor in return for the apartment. The one decision, Cut or Pure, sounds important and is not, so pick the version of the scene you would rather watch. PowerPyx subtitles the mission Go See Dre'Quan.
Before you start

Step-by-step
1. Find Dre'Quan in the studio
Go up the stairs you used in the last mission, through the door at the top and into the recording booth. Wait for Dre'Quan to finish. He asks which hook you prefer; any answer works. Follow him upstairs to Boobie, who explains the job.
2. Pick up from Tyrone
Get into Dre'Quan's car outside and drive to a nearby apartment. Follow him to the room on the second floor, where he talks with a dealer called Tyrone. You can interrupt if you do not want to wait.
3. Cut or Pure

4. The football detour
Dre'Quan takes a different route back to the car through a large park. A short tutorial has you throw a football back to some kids.
5. Make the deal
Drive a short way south, close to the Jack of Hearts. Follow Dre'Quan to the group standing by the cars and hand over the bag when prompted. The buyer tests the product slowly; you can ask him to hurry. When he is done, take back the backpack, which now holds the money.
Tip: both guides say a non-violent finish here earns a Professional bonus.
6. The confrontation
On the way back to the car a man stops you and insists the bag is his. He attacks no matter what you say. Knock him out with melee, then get in the car.

Head for the shop in Southside. A scene starts about halfway there and ends the mission. Back at the apartment, Cal tries and fails to get into the hard drive, and mentions that Brian once had a capable contact in Vice City.

Q: Should you pick Cut or Pure in the GTA 6 Dealer's Choice walkthrough?
A: Pure gives a smooth deal. Cut is noticed by the buyers, but offering it at half price still ends peacefully. PowerPyx and GTABase both say the choice has no effect later.

Q: Who can play Dealer's Choice?
A: Only Jason. Go back to the Jack of Hearts as Jason after Welcome to Vice City.

Q: How much does Dealer's Choice pay?
A: PowerPyx's summary lists $1,500 for selling Pure product, but its own walkthrough says you gain no money either way, and GTABase lists no cash reward. Treat the payout as unconfirmed.

Q: Can you avoid the fight at the end of Dealer's Choice?
A: No. The man who claims the bag attacks whatever you answer. Both guides say to knock him out with melee and drive off.

# Does GTA 6 Have Difficulty Settings? Every Option That Helps

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-difficulty-settings/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- GTA 6 has no difficulty selector: there is no easy, normal or hard mode to choose.
- Two toggles under Settings > Gameplay > Accessibility make the game much easier: Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage.
- Targeting mode, Aim Assist Strength, Shooting Assist and Simplified Mini Games let you tune the rest, and all of them can be changed at any time.

GTA 6 difficulty settings do not include an easy, normal or hard mode: the game has one difficulty, and you adjust it with individual options instead. Two of those options, Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, are easy mode in all but name. Others change how much the game helps you aim, how forgiving button prompts are and how mini-games play. This page lists every option that affects difficulty, where to find it and what to set if you are stuck.
Menu names come from Rockstar's own support page and from a full listing of the options screens published at launch; effects are stated only where two sources agree or where we name the source.
GTA 6 difficulty options at a glance

Option
Where
Values
Effect on difficulty

Accessible Combat
Gameplay &gt; Accessibility
Off / On
Large: enemies deal less damage

Reduced Vehicle Damage
Gameplay &gt; Accessibility
Off / On
Large: vehicles are much harder to wreck

Targeting
Gameplay &gt; Combat
Lock-On / Partial / Free Aim
Large: how much the game aims for you

Aim Assist Strength
Gameplay &gt; Combat
Slider
Medium

Shooting Assist
Gameplay &gt; Combat
Off / On
Medium

Drive-By Assist
Gameplay &gt; Combat
Off / On
Medium, in vehicles

Simplified Mini Games
Gameplay &gt; Accessibility
Off / On
Small: activities only

Tap Assist and Hold Assist
Gameplay &gt; Accessibility
Several levels
Small: button prompts

Auto Drive
Gameplay &gt; Accessibility
Restricted / Unrestricted
Small: driving

There is no difficulty selector
VGC and BGR both state it plainly: you cannot pick a difficulty level in GTA 6. Rockstar's support article on settings lists the menu categories (Control Scheme, Controller, Gameplay, Display, UI, Camera, Audio and Account) and none of them is a difficulty menu.
Why it matters: there is nothing to choose at the start of a new game and nothing you can get wrong. Everything on this page can be changed later from the pause menu.
Where the settings are

Pause the game.
Open Settings.
Use the shoulder buttons to move to the Gameplay tab.
Gameplay has three groups: Combat, Movement and Accessibility.

Rockstar's support page adds that Restore Default and Restore All buttons sit at the bottom of the screen if you want to undo your changes.
Tip: when you change one of the options that affect balance, the game shows a warning that it may significantly change the experience. VGC notes that if you leave without saving, the old values come back, so confirm the change.
Accessible Combat: the main easy-mode switch
Accessible Combat is under Gameplay &gt; Accessibility and is off by default. VGC describes it as reducing the damage enemies do to Jason and Lucia, and names it as one of the two toggles that make up an easy mode. The options listing at Playday.One labels it as making the game far easier.
Why it matters: later missions throw more enemies at you. If a shootout such as the airstrip fight in Slam Dunk keeps ending badly, this is the first thing to switch on.
Reduced Vehicle Damage
The second easy-mode toggle sits in the same group. According to VGC, it makes it much harder to disable a vehicle completely by crashing, although several high-speed crashes will still do it. BGR describes it loosely as turning vehicle damage off; the option's actual name, and VGC's description, show that it reduces damage instead of removing it.
Why it matters: many missions fail or drag when your car dies in a chase. With this on, mistakes at speed cost less. It helps most in escapes from a wanted level.
Targeting: Lock-On, Partial or Free Aim
Under Gameplay &gt; Combat, Targeting has three modes:

Mode
What to expect

Lock-On
The most help: aiming snaps to a target

Partial
A middle setting

Free Aim
No lock; you aim entirely yourself

The names are from the options listing; VGC confirms that lock-on can be switched on to make shooting easier.
Tip: if you are coming from GTA 5's default aiming, start on Lock-On. Move to Partial once fights feel routine. Free Aim suits players who also play shooters.
Aim Assist Strength, Shooting Assist and Quick Draw
Three more Combat options fine-tune gunfights:

Aim Assist Strength. A slider. Playday.One's listing shows it running from 0 to 4 with 4 as the default; BGR describes a 0 to 5 scale. Either way, the highest value is the most help and is where the game starts.
Shooting Assist. Off or On.
Drive-By Assist. Off or On; it applies when shooting from vehicles.
Quick Draw. Off or On; BGR describes it as prioritising a fast draw.

Why it matters: the default settings already lean towards assistance. If combat feels too easy, lowering Aim Assist Strength is the gentlest way to add challenge without touching anything else.
Simplified Mini Games and button assists
The Accessibility group also covers everything that is not combat:

Option
Values
Use it if

Simplified Mini Games
Off / On
Activities such as gym sessions are a barrier

Tap Assist
Off, 2x, 3x, 4x, Hold
Rapid button tapping is hard for you

Hold Assist
Off up to 4x
Long holds are uncomfortable

Hold Delay
0% to 250%
Prompts trigger too fast or too slowly

Aiming, Interact, Nitrous
Hold / Press
You prefer toggles to held buttons

Fishing
Rotate / Hold / Pull
The default fishing input is awkward

Auto Drive
Restricted / Unrestricted
You want the car to drive itself more often

Auto Equip Helmet
Off / On
You ride bikes a lot

BGR mentions that mini-game difficulty can be adjusted, with gym sessions as its example; in the menu that is the Simplified Mini Games switch.
Tip: workouts, fishing and similar activities feed challenges and cheat unlocks. If they are what is stopping you, turn on Simplified Mini Games before you give up on GTA 6 challenges.
Options that help without changing balance
Some settings make the game easier to read without making enemies weaker:

Projectile Arc shows where a thrown object will land.
Map, minimap and in-world marker size can be set to Large.
GPS Voice is off by default and can be set to tones or speech.
Reticle Shape can be Complex, Simple, Dot or None.
High Contrast Shaders and colour adjustments are available under Display.
Camera Shake and cinematic crash and kill cameras can be reduced.
Focus has its own input setting. By default Focus Mode is entered by pressing L3 and R3 together; VGC suggests it for spotting mission items you cannot find.

Why it matters: a lot of "difficulty" in an open-world game is information. Bigger markers and a visible throwing arc fix problems that no damage setting will. More basics are in how to play GTA 6.
What is not confirmed

Trophies and achievements. No source we checked says whether Accessible Combat or Reduced Vehicle Damage affects trophies. Cheats do disable them; these are settings, not cheats, but that is not proof.
A mission skip. Earlier Rockstar games offered a skip after repeated failures. None of the launch guides mentions one in GTA 6.
The exact Aim Assist range. Two outlets report different scales, as noted above.
An "enemy encounters" setting. BGR refers to adjusting enemy encounters; no option with that name appears in the full listing.
A harder mode. Nothing in the menus raises enemy damage or removes checkpoints.

Recommended setups

Story only, minimum stress. Accessible Combat on, Reduced Vehicle Damage on, Targeting on Lock-On, Simplified Mini Games on.
Default with a safety net. Leave everything as it is; switch on Accessible Combat only for a mission you have failed three times, then switch it off again.
Stuck on driving, fine at shooting. Reduced Vehicle Damage on, everything else default.
Want more challenge. Targeting on Free Aim, Aim Assist Strength down, Shooting Assist off, minimap set to Dynamic or Off.
Before any change. Make a manual save, so you can compare. See how to save in GTA 6.

What this means for you
If you were looking for an easy mode, you have one: two switches under Accessibility, available from the first minute and reversible whenever you like. If you were looking for a hard mode, you have to build it yourself by taking assists away. And if you only want the game to be clearer, the UI and navigation options do more than the combat ones. Since missions cannot be replayed (see can you replay missions in GTA 6), there is no score to protect by leaving the assists off.
Playing in first person changes how aiming feels as well; see GTA 6 first-person mode.
What we will add to this page

Whether the easy-mode toggles affect trophies, once two sources confirm it either way.
Our own tested recommendations for Aim Assist Strength in each Targeting mode.
Any difficulty options added by a title update; see GTA 6 updates.

Q: Does GTA 6 have difficulty settings?
A: Not as a single choice. There is no easy, normal or hard mode, but separate options such as Accessible Combat, Reduced Vehicle Damage, Targeting and Aim Assist Strength change how demanding the game is.

Q: How do you turn on easy mode in GTA 6?
A: Pause, open Settings, go to the Gameplay tab and find the Accessibility group. Switch on Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, then save the change when the warning appears.

Q: Can you change the difficulty during the story in GTA 6?
A: Yes. VGC notes that the easy-mode toggles can be switched on or off at any time.

Q: Does GTA 6 have aim assist?
A: Yes. Targeting has three modes, Lock-On, Partial and Free Aim, with a separate Aim Assist Strength slider and a Shooting Assist toggle.

---

# GTA 6 Dubious Provenance Walkthrough: The Halifax Choice

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-dubious-provenance-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Dubious Provenance is a three-part Chapter 3 mission that starts at the bag in the Bayside apartment closet and moves to Capri.
- Giving Halifax the statue earns a Crowex watch and opens parts 2 and 3; refuse and never call him, and those parts are lost.
- Part 3 ends at a storage container with about $2,500 in jewelry and cash and a '32 Hustler to keep or sell.

This GTA 6 Dubious Provenance walkthrough covers all three parts of the statue mission and the three choices in it. Jason and Lucia take the statue to an antique store in Capri to learn what it is. Only the first part is needed for the story, but the later parts hold the money and a long chase. PowerPyx subtitles it Visit the Antique Store.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Dubious Provenance (Chapter 3), in three parts

Playable characters
Jason and Lucia; either can start it

Starts at
The bag in the closet of the Bayside apartment

Then
Capri, Mariana County, on the far west of the map

Requirement
Finish Dealer's Choice

Reward
Crowex watch (part 1); about $2,500 and a '32 Hustler (part 3)

The three choices at a glance

Choice
Option that keeps the mission going
The other option

Give Halifax the statue?
Accept: you get his watch and part 2
Decline: call him later, or lose parts 2 and 3 at the end of Chapter 3

Trust Halifax at the motel?
Trust: part 3 opens
The mission stops short of part 3

Shoot or spare Halifax?
Free choice
Free choice

Objectives

Part 1: go to the antique store; optionally explore Capri together; optionally call Halifax about the statue.
Part 2: get into Evelyn Andrews Antiques; get inside through the window; let Jason in; find the statue; go to the motel; search for Halifax in the motel.
Part 3: go to Maryam's house; chase Halifax; approach Halifax; call Jason.

Step-by-step
Part 1: the antique store

Interact with the bag in the apartment closet.
Drive west to Capri, or take a RydeMe to save time (fast travel guide).
Try the front door of the store. You go upstairs automatically.
The owner, Evelyn Andrews, will not touch the statue. A British dealer, Benedict Halifax, offers to appraise it off the books and leaves his watch as collateral.
Accept or decline. If you accept, the watch can be worn from a wardrobe under Accessories, then Watches.

An optional objective asks you to explore Capri with your partner. Visiting any shop or leaving town clears it.
Part 2: the break-in
Halifax never calls back. Return to the store and wait until Evelyn leaves.

You can force the door, or go in quietly: take the stairs round the back, jump to the lower roof and climb through the window above the air conditioner.
Walk to the door and let Jason in.
Check the drawer of the desk in the north corner. It points to the motel next door.
At the motel, a resident sends you to an upstairs room on the west side. Interact with the door.
After the scene, decide whether to trust Halifax.

Part 3: the chase
After another silence, Evelyn calls. Talk to her at the store; she gives an address in the north-west of town.

Halifax runs for a boat. Jason follows on a Seashark. Get close and hold Square (X on Xbox) to board.
He crashes and runs. Swim to shore and keep after him.
He takes a golf cart. Grab the bike in the yard.
He pepper-sprays Jason, and the game switches to Lucia as Halifax runs into her car. Get out, use Focus (L3 + R3) and shoot him in the leg.
Walk up to him, take out Lucia's phone and call Jason.
When Jason arrives you get the statue back. Shoot or spare Halifax.

Tip: before you leave, empty the storage container. Both guides put it at about $2,500 in jewelry and cash, and the '32 Hustler parked there is yours to keep or sell.
Where players fail

Declining and forgetting. If you refuse Halifax and never phone him, the statue plot closes with the chapter.
Choosing not to trust him. That ends the mission before the chase and the loot.
Losing Halifax in the chase. Each vehicle swap is scripted; keep moving and take the vehicle the guides name at each stage.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Watch
Crowex "Bobby Ambrose" (the two guides spell the model name differently)

Loot
About $2,500 in jewelry and cash

Vehicle
'32 Hustler

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required; PowerPyx says the Halifax call itself is not

Part 1 also unlocks two Jason missions: Here, Kitty Kitty and Boobie Time, whose contact Yasmani pays the best price for jewelry. Full order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: Should you give Halifax the statue in the GTA 6 Dubious Provenance walkthrough?
A: Yes, if you want the whole mission. Accepting gives you his Crowex watch and leads to parts 2 and 3. If you decline you can still call him later, but if you never do, the rest disappears at the end of Chapter 3.

Q: Do you have to trust Halifax at the motel?
A: PowerPyx and GTABase both say trusting him is what lets you play part 3, so choose it if you want the chase and the loot.

Q: Should you shoot or spare Halifax?
A: Either. Both guides call it a free choice and report no consequence.

Q: What do you get for finishing Dubious Provenance?
A: The Crowex watch in part 1, then about $2,500 in jewelry and cash from the storage container in part 3, plus a '32 Hustler parked there.

# GTA 6 Girl's Trip Walkthrough: Find Painkillers for Jason

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-girls-trip-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: confirmed

- Girl's Trip is the longest early Chapter 2 mission: Lucia and Vicki search Port Gellhorn for a dealer called Dunk.
- At the car wash, picking Defuse twice ends the stand-off with the Kolts without a fight and earns Professional reputation.
- Do not destroy Dunk's car in the chase; follow him until he crashes, then drive him back to his trailer.

This GTA 6 Girl's Trip walkthrough takes Lucia from a motel room to a strip club, a boatyard and a car wash in search of real painkillers for Jason. It introduces Vicki, the dealer Dunk and the Kolts gang, and it is the mission that opens up Port Gellhorn. PowerPyx subtitles it Find Painkillers.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Girl's Trip (Chapter 2); GTABase spells it Girls' Trip

Playable character
Lucia

Given by
Vicki

Starts at
Search area at the Starlet Motel, Kelly County

Requirement
Finish Overnight Charges and Just Moved In

Reward
$50 returned by Vicki through BuckMe

Objectives

Ask around the motel about painkillers.
Get the pills from Vicki in Room 10 and take them to Jason.
Go back to Vicki's room.
Drive Vicki's car to Delights.
Look for Dunk: his trailer, the boatyard, the car wash.
Deal with the Kolts.
Follow Dunk and take him home.

Step-by-step
1. Ask Zach
Zach is peering through the windows between your room and reception. He points you to Vicki in Room 10.
2. Buy the pills
Knock on Room 10. Vicki fetches pills from the bathroom and charges $50. VGC notes an optional bong while you wait.
3. Back to Jason
In your room Jason recognises the pills as Zombix, an ordinary over-the-counter product. They are useless to him.
4. Confront Vicki
Return to Room 10. Lucia gets rough with Vicki, who then offers to find the real thing through someone she knows.
5. Delights
Get in Vicki's car and drive west into Port Gellhorn. Park at Delights, the club where she works, and follow her inside. Her boss, Frankie Delight, hands over her pay. Go back to the car.
6. Trailer, then boatyard
Dunk is not at his trailer. Vicki suggests the boatyard, where his friends say he went to the car wash to sell.
7. The car wash
Inside, Dunk is in trouble with the Kolts. He slips out through the shutter and leaves you with them.

Choice
Result

Defuse, twice in a row
The Kolts leave without a fight; you gain Professional reputation (PowerPyx, GTABase)

Provoke, or attack
A fight

Tip: VGC's guide describes the fight route only, so the calm ending is easy to miss. Take Defuse both times.
8. Chase Dunk
Lift the shutter and follow Dunk's car. You are not meant to stop him: he crashes by himself. PowerPyx and GTABase place the crash at a farm; VGC says he ends up in the far paddock beside the reception building at the gun range.
9. Take Dunk home
Vicki talks to the rangers while you put Dunk in the car and drive him to his trailer. He has no painkillers left but says his supplier, "Doctor Bill with the Pill", can get more.
Where players fail

Destroying Dunk's car. VGC lists this as a mission failure. Follow; do not ram or shoot.
Picking a fight you do not need. Defuse saves health and ammo.
Losing the chase. Stay on the road behind him until the crash scene.

Optional goals and rewards

Item
Details

Reward
$50 back from Vicki via BuckMe

Reputation
Professional, for defusing the Kolts

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

Afterwards the chapter opens up: Moses, New Look, How Do I Look? and the waiting mission Painkiller Supplier all become available. GTABase suggests doing Moses first so you have your own car. Full order: GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you start the GTA 6 Girl's Trip walkthrough?
A: Finish Overnight Charges and Just Moved In. A search area appears at the Starlet Motel; talk to Zach near reception, then knock on Room 10 to meet Vicki.

Q: Should you choose Defuse or Provoke with the Kolts?
A: PowerPyx and GTABase recommend Defuse twice in a row: the Kolts leave and you earn Professional reputation. Provoking or attacking starts a fight.

Q: Do you get the $50 back from Vicki?
A: Yes. PowerPyx and GTABase both list $50 returned through BuckMe as the mission reward.

Q: Is it Girl's Trip or Girls' Trip?
A: PowerPyx and VGC write Girl's Trip; GTABase writes Girls' Trip. It is the same mission.

---

# GTA 6 Heists: Both Story Heists, Setup Missions and Robberies

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-heists/
Updated: 2026-11-21
Status: partly

- GTA 6 has two story heists: the Cartel Heist at Sinfrontera National Bank in Chapter 3 and the VCIA Takedown at the airport in Chapter 4.
- Each is a chain of setup missions; walkthrough lists tag eight missions for the Cartel Heist and fifteen for the VCIA Takedown.
- Heists cannot be replayed, and their payouts, crew options and approaches are not yet confirmed by two guides.

GTA 6 heists come in two sizes: two big story heists, the Cartel Heist and the VCIA Takedown, and a long list of smaller robberies you can run between missions. The story heists are multi-mission operations that close out Chapter 3 and dominate Chapter 4. This page lists every setup mission in order, the smaller jobs that lead up to them, the tools and safe codes confirmed so far, and what guides have not yet agreed on.
Mission names and order here match in two independent walkthrough lists, PowerPyx and GTABase. Where only one source reports something, we say so.
GTA 6 heists at a glance

The Cartel Heist
VCIA Takedown

Chapter
3 (the chapter's last mission)
4 (late in the chapter)

Target
Sinfrontera National Bank
